statementIssues.note: States "dehydration reduced short-term glycogen restoration in cited studies"; the source says the 4 h effect was only "close to being significant" and that the cited studies concluded dehydration "did not impair muscle glycogen storage". The rehydration advice itself is sound, but the evidential basis is misstated.

Repeats the C11 overstatement ("cited studies found dehydration reduced short-term glycogen restoration"). On polyphenols it cites only the null tart cherry RL study and omits the positive soccer tart cherry trial reported on the same page of the same review.

"Playing time drives weekly load, so plans should reflect each athlete's actual load" is presented as evidence-based. C21 is an association in one soccer team, and scaling nutrition to load is professional judgment. recommendedDirection labels it as judgment, but the bottomLine does not.
Gives "6 to 8 g/kg BM carbohydrate" without the per-day unit shown in the UEFA table.

The morning body weight, thirst and urine check comes from UEFA's heat and stressful-environment section for use without specialist support. Using it as a routine travel check is reasonable but unlabeled extrapolation.

"Do not use alcohol as recovery hydration" is broader than the source, which says only that beer is inadvisable as the sole rehydration source after a deficit of 1.5% body mass or more. The second sentence states the source accurately.

tierNote: Moderate is defensible for the food-first fueling, fluid and pre-match meal core. That guidance rests on a consensus statement and a review that agree with each other, and the rationale states the gaps in population, travel and individualization. Supplement tension is acknowledged and the tier is not Higher.

criticalFailures.note: The claim drops the near-significant (non-significant) qualifier and the contrary 15 h finding. It turns a null-leaning finding into "dehydration reduced short-term glycogen restoration in cited studies" in an action.

usefulnessNote: A nutrition practitioner gets a usable food-first plan quickly: carbohydrate ranges for congested periods, pre and post-competition amounts, gut-comfort meal guidance, food-safety and supplement guardrails. Transferability limits are stated honestly. The hydration overstatement does not change the advice to rehydrate, so it does not mislead the decision. Subgroup individualization is clearly labeled as judgment.
suggestedDrafterFixes: When an excerpt ends mid-sentence, read the rest of the sentence and the next one. Carry any significance qualifier (e.g. 'close to being significant', 'not significant') and any contrary finding into the claim.
Do not phrase a claim as an observed effect ('X reduced Y') when the source reports a non-significant or trend-level result. Use 'tended to' or 'non-significant' wording.
When a review reports both positive and null trials for an intervention, cite both in evidenceTension instead of only the side that fits the tension.
When a claim is removed, repair later claims that refer back to it ('In that case study') so each claim names its own study design and sample.
Keep units, including per-day, when copying dose ranges into actions.
Apply 'Professional judgment' labeling to bottomLine text as well as to recommendedDirection and actions.
